title: The Moon, Through the Glass, Still Unsure

content.question: Is the moon really the colour the sky suggests at dusk, or does the telescope show something the eye has been keeping from me?
content.method: At dusk, with the sky still holding its last blue, I sat on the lookout rock beside the telescope and kept my eyes on the moon through the lens, one patient session, pretending I was not waiting for it to show its colour. I compared what the glass gave me against what I saw with my own eyes, and I looked away and back again several times, because a colour that changes when you look at it is not yet a colour.
content.result: The moon did not give up its colour. Through the glass it was a pale, cool grey with a faint warmth at the lower edge, and the warmth vanished whenever I looked straight at it. I am recording this as unresolved. The moon is hiding something, and I have noted the exact hour so that I may return to it when it forgets to be careful.
